articles.title: Mutual funds' Nifty 50 allocation falls to 21-year low in Q2
articles.excerpt:
Domestic mutual funds’ allocation to Nifty 50 stocks fell to a 21-year low in the September quarter, slipping below 50 per cent for the first time in over two decades, as fund portfolios continued to expand beyond the country’s largest benchmark companies.

The share of Nifty 50 stocks in mutual funds’ holdings of NSE-listed equities declined by two percentage points to 49.4 per cent from 51.4 per cent in June, according to the National Stock Exchange’s (NSE) India Ownership Tracker report. articles.excerpt:
Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) increased their investments in government securities under the Fully Accessible Route (FAR) by nearly ₹8,000 crore in the first week of November, amid a strengthening rupee and easing bond yields.
